whatItDoes: Shall the measure amending the Bylaws of the El Camino Healthcare District to limit District Directors to four four-year terms be adopted?

ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 1 — DETERMINISTIC OCR
Impartial Analysis — Measure S — El Camino Healthcare District — Term Limits

California law permits a district’s governing body to propose a measure to limit the number of
terms a member of the governing body may serve. Here, the Board of Directors of the El
Camino Healthcare District (District) has placed on the ballot a Measure to amend the District
Bylaws to limit District Directors to serving four (4) four-year terms. The District currently has
no limit on the number of terms a Director may serve.

If a majority of voters approve this Measure, the District Bylaws will be amended to provide
that:

e For terms beginning on or after December 1, 2026, no person may serve more than four
full terms as a District Director;

e If for any reason a District Director serves a partial term—such as when a Director is
appointed to fill a vacancy—that partial term shall not be counted as a term for purposes
of the four-term limit; and

e Terms served prior to December 1, 2026, whether full or partial, are not included toward
the maximum number of terms.

A “yes” vote is a vote to amend the District Bylaws to prohibit District Directors from serving
more than four full terms, for terms beginning on or after December 1, 2026.

A “no” vote is a vote to not amend the District Bylaws.
